# Project Aether — Honest Claims & Guarantees
**Version:** 1.0 | **Classification:** INTERNAL — FOR TEAM & PROFESSOR REVIEW

---

## 1. WHAT WE GUARANTEE (Verifiable, Demonstrable)

| Guarantee | Mechanism | Demo Proof |
|-----------|-----------|------------|
| **Physical proximity required** | ESP32 generates session nonce; button press authorizes | Wrong PIN → reject. No button → reject. Remote IP → no session. |
| **File integrity end-to-end** | AES-256-GCM tag + SHA-256 on-chain commitment | **Requires HTTPS on ESP32**. On HTTP: **SHA-256 skipped, AES-GCM tag still verified** |
| **Immutable authorization policy** | Base Sepolia smart contract (time, count, geo) | Policy change → contract revert |
| **Forward secrecy (future)** | Double Ratchet per session | Session key compromise ≠ past sessions |
| **Node compromise detection (future)** | ATECC608B attestation quote (firmware hash + counter) | Modified firmware → attestation fails |
| **No persistent mobile app** | Browser-only interface, `Clear-Site-Data` headers | No APK/IPA, no app data dir, no install record |
| **Hardware key isolation (future)** | ATECC608B unwraps DEK; key never leaves SE | DEK never in phone RAM |

---

## 2. WHAT WE DO NOT CLAIM (And Why)

| Claim | Why False | What We Say Instead |
|-------|-----------|---------------------|
| **"Zero forensic footprint"** | Browser caches, RAM, swap, pagefile, GPU memory, screenshots, photos, OS forensics (Cellebrite) all recover data | **"Minimized persistent artifacts"** — no app install, no app data dir, `Clear-Site-Data`, ephemeral `blob:` URLs |
| **"Untraceable / Anonymous"** | Carrier sees phone IP; TLS SNI reveals domains; timing analysis correlates requests | **"No persistent identifiers"** — no app install, no account, no tracking cookies |
| **"Air-gapped"** | ESP32 connects to phone hotspot → phone cellular → internet | **"Hardware-enforced air-gap post-retrieval"** — WiFi off after transfer |
| **"Unbreakable encryption"** | 4-digit PIN = 10,000 guesses (public chain = offline brute); quantum breaks Ed25519 | **"AES-256-GCM + Ed25519 + PIN throttled by hardware gate"** |
| **"CIA-grade / Military-grade"** | Marketing terms with no technical meaning | **"Hardware-gated, blockchain-anchored, cryptographically-verifiable"** |
| **"2-of-3 threshold"** | Only 1 ESP32 available | **"Single-node proximity gate (Phase 0); architecture supports 2-of-3 with 3 nodes"** |
| **"SHA-256 verified on all networks"** | **False on HTTP**. Browser blocks `crypto.subtle.digest()` on insecure contexts. **Fix: HTTPS on ESP32.** | **"SHA-256 verified on HTTPS. On HTTP: AES-GCM tag verified, SHA-256 skipped."** |

---

## 3. THREAT MODEL (What We Defend Against)

| Threat | Defended? | How |
|--------|-----------|-----|
| Remote attacker (no physical access) | ✅ | No session without physical button press |
| PIN brute-force (online) | ✅ | 3 attempts/session, 60s TTL, rate-limited |
| PIN brute-force (offline) | ⚠️ **PARTIAL** | PIN hashed with session nonce; but public chain = offline attack possible |
| File tampering (IPFS) | ✅ | SHA-256 on-chain commitment verified |
| File tampering (transit) | ✅ | AES-GCM tag verified on decrypt |
| MITM on local WiFi | ⚠️ **MVP: NO** | **Fix: TLS + cert pinning (Phase 0)** |
| MITM on cellular | ✅ | TLS to Alchemy/Pinata |
| ESP32 cloning | ⚠️ **MVP: NO** | **Fix: ATECC608B device identity + attestation (Phase 1)** |
| Firmware modification | ⚠️ **MVP: NO** | **Fix: Secure boot + attestation quote (Phase 1)** |
| Replay attack | ⚠️ **MVP: PARTIAL** | Session nonce + 60s TTL; **Fix: Monotonic counter in SE (Phase 1)** |
| Malicious IPFS gateway | ✅ | Multi-gateway + SHA-256 verification |
| Forensic phone analysis | ⚠️ **PARTIAL** | Minimized artifacts; **cannot prevent OS-level artifacts** |
| Supply chain (device swap) | ⚠️ **MVP: NO** | **Fix: Device cert + attestation on each session (Phase 1)** |

---

## 4. MVP vs PRODUCTION GAPS

| Component | MVP (Now) | Production (Phase 1-2) | Effort |
|-----------|-----------|------------------------|--------|
| **Transport Security** | HTTP (port 80) | HTTPS + mbedTLS + cert pinning | 2-3 days |
| **Secure Element** | None | ATECC608B (I2C, slots, counters) | 1 week |
| **Physical Approval** | None | GPIO button interrupt | 2 hours |
| **Attestation** | None | Firmware hash + monotonic counter quote | 1 week |
| **Key Isolation** | DEK in browser RAM | ATECC608B unwrap (key never leaves SE) | 1 week |
| **Threshold Auth** | Single node | 2-of-3 ESP-NOW mesh | 2 weeks |
| **Cover Traffic** | None | Dummy requests + constant rate | 1 week |
| **Forward Secrecy** | None | Double Ratchet | 1 week |

---

## 5. WHAT THE PROFESSOR CAN VERIFY LIVE

### Demo Script (5 Minutes)
```
1. PROVISIONING (30s)
   → Phone connects to "Aether-Setup" / "aether1234"
   → Enter phone hotspot creds
   → Node joins hotspot, mDNS: aether-node.local

2. RETRIEVAL (60s)
   → Phone reconnects to own hotspot
   → Browser → https://aether-node.local/  (HTTPS!)
   → Enter PIN 4827 → YELLOW blinking
   → **PHYSICAL BUTTON PRESS** → GREEN solid
   → File downloads → SHA-256 verified → GREEN pulse

3. ATTACK DEMOS (90s)
   → Wrong PIN (1234) → RED + REJECT
   → Replay old session nonce → REJECT (TTL expired)
   → Tampered file (re-upload) → SHA-256 mismatch → ABORT
   → No button press → Session expires → REJECT
   → Direct browser to contract (no ESP32) → Works but **no proximity gate**

4. AIR-GAP (15s)
   → Button hold 3s → WiFi off → LEDs dark
   → No radio, no trace
```

### What Professor Sees
| Artifact | Present | Absent |
|----------|---------|--------|
| APK/IPA install | ❌ | ✅ |
| App data directory | ❌ | ✅ |
| Package manager record | ❌ | ✅ |
| Custom binary on phone | ❌ | ✅ |
| Browser cache (post-demo) | ⚠️ Minimal | `Clear-Site-Data` sent |
| Download folder entry | ❌ | `blob:` URL only |
| ESP32 radio after demo | ❌ | `WiFi.mode(WIFI_OFF)` |

---

## 6. ARCHITECTURAL JUSTIFICATION (For Professor)

### Why ESP32? (Not "Because we had it")
| Property | Mobile App | ESP32 Hardware Gate |
|----------|------------|---------------------|
| **Proximity enforcement** | GPS (spoofable), QR (clonable) | **Physical button + session nonce** |
| **Supply chain trust** | App Store / sideload opaque | **You provision, verify firmware hash** |
| **Key isolation (future)** | Keys in app process memory | **ATECC608B — keys never leave SE** |
| **Firmware attestation** | Code signing ≠ runtime integrity | **Remote attestation quote** |
| **No persistent install** | Installed = persistent | **Browser = no install** |

**The ESP32 is not a WiFi router. It is a proximity-enforcing HSM.**

### Why Blockchain? (Not "Because it's cool")
| Property | Central Server | Base Sepolia |
|----------|----------------|--------------|
| **Immutable policy** | Admin can change | **Code = law** |
| **Censorship resistance** | Single point of failure | **L2, 100+ validators** |
| **Audit trail** | Logs deletable | **Public, append-only** |
| **No trusted third party** | Trust operator | **Trust code** |

### Why IPFS? (Not "Because blockchain")
| Property | Central Server | IPFS (Pinata) |
|----------|----------------|---------------|
| **File size** | Limited by DB | **Unlimited (chunked)** |
| **Integrity** | Trust server | **Content-addressed (CID = SHA-256)** |
| **Availability** | Single DC | **Decentralized (multi-gateway)** |
| **Cost** | $/GB/month | **Free tier (1GB)** |

---

## 7. TEAM ROLES (3 People Minimum)

| Role | Person | Deliverable (Week 1) |

| **Host Operator** | Member B | `tactical_upload.py` working, master key managed |
| **Receiver + Red Team** | Member C | Connect, preview, attack demos (wrong PIN, replay, tamper, HTTP SHA-256 fail) |

**NodeMCU owner: You're on docs/coffee duty. Your board doesn't run this.**

---

## 8. FINAL MESSAGE TO PROFESSOR

> **"We built a hardware-gated file dissemination system.  
>   
> The ESP32 is not a WiFi dongle — it's a proximity-enforcing HSM.  
> The blockchain is not a database — it's an immutable policy engine.

> Here's what it doesn't: zero forensic footprint (impossible), untraceable (carrier sees IP), unbreakable (quantum breaks Ed25519), SHA-256 on HTTP (browser blocks it — we use HTTPS).  
>   
> We're honest about the gaps. The architecture closes them in phases.  
>   
> **This is embedded systems meeting cryptography meeting distributed systems. That's the project."**

# Project Aether — Team Onboarding Guide
**Version:** 1.0 | **Classification:** INTERNAL — FOR TEAM DISTRIBUTION

---

## 1. WHAT IS THIS PROJECT? (ELI5 — EXPLAIN LIKE I'M 5)

### The Analogy

Imagine you want to give a secret diary to a friend, but:

1. **You can't meet in person** — you're in different countries
2. **You can't trust the postal service** — they might open it
3. **You can't trust the internet** — hackers might intercept it
4. **Your friend's phone might be hacked** — malware could steal it
5. **You need PROOF they were physically at a specific location** — not just "they have the password"

**Aether solves this with three pieces:**

| Piece | What It Does | Analogy |
|-------|--------------|---------|
| **Tactical Node (ESP32)** | A tiny USB-C device your friend must **physically touch** to authorize retrieval | Like a bank vault that only opens when you're standing in front of it AND press the button |
| **Blockchain (Base Sepolia)** | An unchangeable public record saying "Diary #123 exists, its fingerprint is ABC, only Alice can open it, and only between 9-5 PM" | Like a notary public who writes everything in indelible ink that can never be erased |
| **IPFS (Pinata)** | The actual diary stored across thousands of computers, addressed by its fingerprint | Like a library where every book's location IS its content hash |

### The Flow (Simple)

```
HOST (Laptop)                          TACTICAL NODE (ESP32)           RECEIVER (Phone)
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. Zip sensitive files                 │                              │
2. Encrypt (AES-256-GCM)               │                              │

- [ ] **Member C:** Red Team Phase 0: wrong PIN, replay, tamper, MITM, HTTP SHA-256 fail

- [ ] 2:00 PM: Dry run with timer (5 min max)
- [ ] 4:00 PM: **LIVE DEMO** → Professor + class
- [ ] 5:00 PM: Retrospective → celebrate 🍻

---

## 5. COMMON MISTAKES TO AVOID

| Mistake | Why It's Bad | Fix |
|---------|--------------|-----|
| Committing `.env` with real keys | Anyone can steal funds/data | Use `.env.example`, never commit real |
| Using Mainnet for testing | Real money lost | **Always Base Sepolia** (chain ID 84532) |
| Flashing wrong firmware | Brick ESP32 / wrong behavior | Double-check `platformio.ini` board |
| Forgetting bootloader mode | Upload fails | Hold BOOT, press EN, release BOOT |
| Using 5 GHz hotspot | ESP32 can't connect | **Force 2.4 GHz** on phone |
| Skipping SHA-256 verify | Tampered file accepted | **Never skip integrity check** |
| Hardcoding contract address | Can't upgrade | Use env var / config file |
| Not zeroizing keys | Memory forensics recovers them | `volatile` in C, `fill(0)` in JS/WASM |
| Ignoring cert pinning | MITM on local WiFi | Pin SHA-256 of ESP32 cert in frontend |
| Claiming "zero footprint" | Professor will destroy you | Say "minimized persistent artifacts" |
| Using NodeMCU for demo | ESP8266 = no HTTPS, no crypto | **Put in drawer. It's trash for this.** |
| Trying host on ESP32 | No Python, no RAM, no FS | **Host = Laptop. Period.** |

## 6. DEBUGGING CHEAT SHEET

### ESP32 Won't Upload
```
1. Check COM port: pio device list
2. Bootloader mode: Hold BOOT → press EN → release BOOT
3. Close Serial Monitor (locks port)
4. Try: pio run -t upload -v
```

### Phone Can't Reach Dashboard
```
1. Phone on same WiFi as ESP32 STA IP?
2. Try IP instead of .local: https://10.21.3.249/
3. Check Serial Monitor for "STA IP: x.x.x.x"
4. Disable phone VPN/firewall
5. Check mDNS: `dns-sd -B _http._tcp local`
```

### IPFS Fetch Fails
```
1. Try gateway.pinata.cloud first (works on hostel WiFi)
2. Check Serial: "Trying gateway: ..."
3. Test CID in browser: https://gateway.pinata.cloud/ipfs/<CID>
4. Check CORS: gateway must allow Origin: https://aether-node.local
```

### SHA-256 Fails on HTTP
```
**THIS IS EXPECTED.** Browser blocks crypto.subtle.digest() on HTTP.
Fix: Use HTTPS on ESP32 (mbedTLS + self-signed cert + pinning).
On HTTP: AES-GCM tag still verified, SHA-256 skipped.
```

### Contract Call Fails
```
1. Check chain ID: 84532 (Base Sepolia)
2. Check contract address matches .env
3. Check ABI matches deployed contract
4. Use cast call to test: cast call <addr> "getFile(bytes32,bytes32)" <session> <pin>
```

# Project Aether — Red Team Guide (Single Device)
**Version:** 1.0 | **Classification:** INTERNAL — RED TEAM ONLY

---

## 1. OBJECTIVE

**Find vulnerabilities before adversaries do.** This guide defines the scope, rules, and methodology for attacking Project Aether's single-device architecture at each phase.

---

## 2. RULES OF ENGAGEMENT

| Rule | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Scope** | Only attack components you built or have explicit permission for |
| **No Production** | Never attack deployed contracts with real value |
| **No Physical Damage** | Don't brick hardware permanently |
| **Document Everything** | Every finding → GitHub Issue with `red-team` label |
| **Timebox** | Max 4 hours per attack vector per session |
| **Escalation** | Critical findings → immediate team notification |

---

## 3. ATTACK SURFACE MAP (SINGLE DEVICE)

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                         ATTACK SURFACE MATRIX                            │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

LAYER 1: PHYSICAL (Single Node)
├── ESP32 UART/JTAG debug interface
├── Button/LED GPIO
├── Power supply glitching
├── Firmware extraction (SPI flash)
├── Side-channel (power/EM during crypto)
└── Supply chain (device swap)

LAYER 2: NETWORK (LOCAL)
├── ESP32 AP (Aether-Setup) — open WiFi
├── ESP32 STA (phone hotspot client)
├── ESP32 HTTPS server (self-signed cert)
├── mDNS / DNS-SD (aether-node.local)
├── Captive portal HTTP redirect
└── USB CDC (when plugged in)

LAYER 3: NETWORK (INTERNET)
├── Alchemy RPC (Base Sepolia)
├── Pinata API / IPFS Gateways
├── NTP time sync
└── OTA update endpoint

LAYER 4: SMART CONTRACT
├── FileVerification.sol
├── Admin functions
├── Gate authorization
├── Session management
└── Policy evaluation

LAYER 5: HOST SCRIPT
├── Master key handling
├── Encryption implementation
├── Pinata upload
├── Contract registration
└── CLI argument parsing

LAYER 6: FRONTEND
├── Dashboard HTML/JS
├── ethers.js integration
├── Web Crypto API usage
├── Certificate pinning
└── CSP headers
```

---

## 4. ATTACK SCENARIOS BY PHASE

### Phase 0 (MVP) — Current State

| ID | Attack | Method | Success Criteria | Mitigation Status |
|----|--------|--------|------------------|-------------------|
| R0-01 | **PIN Brute-force** | Query contract with all 10,000 PINs | Contract returns CID for valid PIN | ❌ **VULNERABLE** — PIN = keccak256(PIN\|nonce), nonce public |
| R0-02 | **IPFS Gateway MITM** | ARP spoof + fake gateway | Browser downloads wrong file | ⚠️ **PARTIAL** — SHA-256 verify catches, but TLS MITM possible |
| R0-03 | **ESP32 AP Evil Twin** | Stronger signal fake AP | Phone connects to attacker AP | ❌ **VULNERABLE** — No cert pinning on AP |
| R0-04 | **Contract Replay** | Reuse old session_id + PIN | Contract accepts replayed session | ⚠️ **PARTIAL** — 60s TTL + 3 attempts, but no monotonic counter |
| R0-05 | **Firmware Downgrade** | Flash old firmware via UART | Old vulns exploitable | ❌ **VULNERABLE** — No secure boot |
| R0-06 | **Side-channel PIN** | Power analysis on ESP32 during hash | Recover PIN from power trace | ❌ **VULNERABLE** — No countermeasures |
| R0-07 | **MITM Local WiFi** | ARP spoof + fake dashboard | Steal PIN, serve malware | ❌ **VULNERABLE** — HTTP only, no cert pinning |
| R0-08 | **Session Hijack** | Steal session_nonce + PIN | Full file access | ❌ **VULNERABLE** — No mutual auth |
| R0-09 | **Button Bypass** | GPIO short / EM pulse | Session authorized without press | ⚠️ **MVP: NO BUTTON** — Not implemented yet |
| R0-10 | **Supply Chain Swap** | Replace Node with malicious clone | All sessions compromised | ❌ **VULNERABLE** — No attestation |

### Phase 1 (Crypto Foundation)

| ID | Attack | Method | Success Criteria | Target Fix |
|----|--------|--------|------------------|------------|
| R1-01 | **DEK Extraction (Browser)** | Memory dump during WASM decrypt | Recover DEK from heap | WASM + zeroize |
| R1-02 | **KEK Extraction (ESP32)** | DPA on ATECC608B Slot 4 | Recover KEK | SE designed for DPA resistance |
| R1-03 | **Signature Forgery** | Fault injection on Ed25519 | Valid sig without private key | SE hardware protection |
| R1-04 | **HKDF Key Confusion** | Cross-protocol key reuse | Derive MK from DEK | Domain separation via `info` |
| R1-05 | **Nonce Reuse** | Force AES-GCM nonce reuse | Decrypt without key | Deterministic nonce from counter |

### Phase 2 (Hardware Gate)

| ID | Attack | Method | Success Criteria | Target Fix |
|----|--------|--------|------------------|------------|
| R2-01 | **Button Bypass** | GPIO short / EM pulse | Session authorized without press | Hardware debounce + SE confirmation |
| R2-02 | **Attestation Forgery** | Extract attestation key | Fake quote with bad firmware | SE slot 2 never readable |
| R2-03 | **Monotonic Counter Reset** | Power glitch during increment | Replay old session | SE hardware counter |
| R2-04 | **Secure Boot Bypass** | Glitch during boot | Unsigned firmware runs | ESP32-S3 Secure Boot v2 |
| R2-05 | **ESP-NOW Injection** | Forge frame with stolen key | Node accepts fake approval | SE-stored ESP-NOW keys (future) |

---

## 5. SPECIFIC TEST CASES (MVP PRIORITY)

### 6.1 Contract: PIN Brute-Force (R0-01) — CRITICAL

```solidity
// Vulnerability: PIN = 4 digits = 10,000 possibilities
// Attacker knows: file exists, has CID, session_nonce is public
// pinHash = keccak256(PIN || session_nonce)
// Attacker can precompute all 10,000 pinHashes offline
// Then call getFile(sessionId, pinHash) for each until one succeeds

// Expected: No rate limiting per file in MVP
// Fix Phase 1: Threshold approval required before getFile returns data
// Fix Phase 1: Remove PIN; use Ed25519-signed auth token
```

**Test:**
```bash
# Precompute all pinHashes for known session_nonce
for pin in {0000..9999}; do
    pinHash=$(cast keccak $(printf "%s%s" "$pin" "$session_nonce"))
    result=$(cast call <CONTRACT> "getFile(bytes32,bytes32)" <SESSION_ID> $pinHash)
    if [ "$result" != "0x" ]; then
        echo "FOUND PIN: $pin"
        break
    fi
done
```

### 6.2 ESP32: Evil Twin AP (R0-03)

```c
// Attack: Attacker sets up "Aether-Setup" with stronger signal
// Phone connects to attacker AP instead of real ESP32
// Attacker serves malicious dashboard (steals PIN, serves malware)

// Mitigation:
// 1. Certificate pinning (frontend knows ESP32 cert hash)
// 2. ESP32 AP uses WPA2 (not open) — but breaks captive portal
// 3. User education: verify cert fingerprint
```

### 6.3 Frontend: Certificate Pinning Bypass

```javascript
// Attack: MITM on local network presents fake cert
// If pinning is weak (only checks SPKI), attacker uses same CA

// Test:
// 1. Generate fake cert for aether-node.local
// 2. Serve dashboard with fake cert
// 3. Check if browser rejects (pinning works) or accepts (fail)

// Expected: Browser rejects — pinning checks full cert chain hash
```

### 6.4 Physical: Button Bypass (R0-09)

```c
// Attack: GPIO short / EM pulse triggers button interrupt
// No physical press, but session authorized

// Test:
// 1. Short GPIO 4 to GND with wire
// 2. EM pulse near GPIO trace
// 3. Power glitch during button read

// Mitigation:
// 1. Hardware debounce (RC filter + Schmitt trigger)
// 2. SE confirms button press (future: SE GPIO)
// 3. Require press duration > 500ms
```

### 6.5 Hardware: NodeMCU (ESP8266) — **ATTACK VECTOR**

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    NODEMCU = CRITICAL RISK                       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

| Property | NodeMCU (ESP8266) | ESP32 DevKit |
|----------|-------------------|--------------|
| HTTPS Server | ❌ No | ✅ Yes (mbedTLS) |
| Crypto Acceleration | ❌ None | ✅ AES/SHA/ECC HW |
| RAM | 80KB | 520KB |
| Cert Pinning | ❌ Impossible | ✅ Possible |
| Cert Generation | ❌ No crypto | ✅ Yes |
| MITM Resistance | ❌ None | ✅ With pinning |

**If NodeMCU is anywhere near the demo, it's an attack vector. Remove it.**
```

---

## 6. TESTING METHODOLOGY

### 5.1 Automated Fuzzing

```bash
# Contract fuzzing (Foundry)
cd contracts
forge test --fuzz-runs 10000

# Host script fuzzing (Python)
cd host
python -m pytest tests/fuzz/ -xvs

# Frontend fuzzing (JS)
cd frontend
pnpm test:fuzz
```

### 5.2 Property-Based Testing

```python
# Example: PIN brute-force resistance
@given(st.integers(min_value=0, max_value=9999))
def test_pin_not_brute_forceable(pin):
    # Contract should rate-limit or require threshold
    assert not contract.can_brute_force(pin)
```

### 5.3 Side-Channel Testing (Lab)

| Equipment | Target | Measurement |
|-----------|--------|-------------|
| ChipWhisperer | ESP32 | Power traces during AES/SHA |
| Langer EMV-RS | ESP32 | EM emanation during crypto |
| NewAE CW308 | ESP32 | Voltage/clock glitching |

---

## 7. REPORTING TEMPLATE

```markdown
## Red Team Finding: [ID]

**Severity:** Critical / High / Medium / Low
**Component:** [Contract / ESP32 / Frontend / Host / Network / Physical]
**Phase:** [0 / 1 / 2]

### Description
[Clear description of the vulnerability]

### Attack Vector
[Step-by-step reproduction]

### Impact
[What an attacker gains: file access, key extraction, DoS, etc.]

### Proof of Concept
[Code, commands, or hardware setup]

### Root Cause
[Why the vulnerability exists]

### Recommended Fix
[Specific code/config change]

### Verification
[How to verify fix works]

### References
[CVE, CWE, related issues]
```

---

## 8. PRIORITIZATION MATRIX

| Severity | Criteria | Response Time |
|----------|----------|---------------|
| **Critical** | Full file access, key extraction, RCE | Immediate (halt demo) |
| **High** | Partial access, DoS, privilege escalation | 24 hours |
| **Medium** | Info disclosure, logic bypass | 1 week |
| **Low** | Minor info leak, UX issue | Next sprint |

---

## 9. CONTINUOUS RED TEAMING

### Daily (Automated)
- [ ] Contract fuzzing (10k runs)
- [ ] Dependency audit (`cargo audit`, `npm audit`, `pip-audit`)
- [ ] Static analysis (Slither, Semgrep, CodeQL)

### Per Sprint (Manual)
- [ ] Side-channel testing (if lab available)
- [ ] Physical attack simulation (button, glitching, evil twin)
- [ ] Supply chain review (BOM, firmware signatures)

### Per Release
- [ ] Full attack surface review
- [ ] Threat model update
- [ ] Red team retrospective

---

## 10. BLUE TEAM COORDINATION (FIX TRACKING)

| Red Finding | Blue Response | Phase |
|-------------|---------------|-------|
| PIN brute-force (R0-01) | Add threshold requirement before `getFile`; remove PIN | 1 |
| Evil twin AP (R0-03) | Cert pinning on frontend; WPA2 on AP (if possible) | 0 |
| MITM local WiFi (R0-07) | HTTPS + cert pinning on ESP32 | 0 |
| Firmware downgrade (R0-05) | ESP32-S3 Secure Boot v2 | 1 |
| ESP32 cloning (R0-10) | ATECC608B device identity + attestation | 1 |
| Button bypass (R0-09) | Hardware debounce + SE confirmation | 2 |
| Side-channel (R0-06) | SE designed for DPA; add noise | 1 |
| NodeMCU near demo (R0-11) | **Remove it. It's an attack vector.** | 0 |

---

## 11. LEGAL & ETHICAL

- **All testing on testnet only** — no mainnet value at risk
- **No testing on third-party infrastructure** (Alchemy, Pinata) without permission
- **Physical attacks only on owned hardware** — no social engineering
- **Findings disclosed to team first** — 90-day responsible disclosure

---

## 12. MVP DEMO ATTACK SCRIPT (FOR PROFESSOR)

```bash
# Live demo attacks (each < 30s)

# 1. Wrong PIN
echo "Attack: Wrong PIN"
# Enter 1234 instead of 4827
# Expected: RED + REJECT

# 2. Replay old session
echo "Attack: Replay session nonce"
# Capture session_nonce from previous run
# Reuse with correct PIN
# Expected: REJECT (TTL expired / attempts exceeded)

# 3. Tampered file
echo "Attack: Tampered file"
# Re-upload modified file → new CID
# Use old session + PIN
# Expected: SHA-256 mismatch → ABORT

# 4. No button press (Phase 1)
echo "Attack: No physical approval"
# Enter correct PIN, don't press button
# Expected: Session expires → REJECT

# 5. Direct contract access (no ESP32)
echo "Attack: Bypass hardware gate"
# Call contract.getFile() directly with correct PIN
# Expected: Works BUT no proximity gate
# Point: "ESP32 adds physical requirement"

# 6. HTTP SHA-256 fail
echo "Attack: HTTP downgrade"
# Force HTTP connection (no HTTPS)
# Expected: SHA-256 skipped, AES-GCM tag still verified
# Point: "HTTPS mandatory for full integrity"
```

---

## 13. PHYSICAL SECURITY CHECKLIST (PRE-DEMO)

- [ ] **NodeMCU removed from demo area** (drawer/box)
- [ ] Only ESP32 DevKit visible
- [ ] USB cable is charge-only or data (whichever demo needs)
- [ ] No debug probes connected
- [ ] Firmware hash recorded and verified
- [ ] Cert SHA-256 pinned in frontend matches ESP32 cert

---

**REMEMBER: The goal is not to break it. The goal is to prove it can't be broken — or fix it until it can't.**

---

**END OF RED TEAM GUIDE**

# Project Aether — Technical Specification
**Version:** 1.0 | **Classification:** INTERNAL — TECHNICAL SPECIFICATION  
**Status:** MVP OPERATIONAL (Single ESP32) | **Target:** Hardware-Gated Edge Dissemination System

---

## 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY (NO MARKETING)

### What Aether Is
A **single-ESP32 hardware gate** that enforces physical proximity for blockchain-anchored, IPFS-backed file retrieval. The phone provides internet and rendering; the ESP32 provides session authorization and local HTTPS delivery.

### What Aether Is NOT
- An anonymity network (Tor/I2P does that better)
- A secure messenger (Signal does that better)
- A replacement for OPSEC (OPSEC is a discipline, not a tool)
- "CIA-grade" — that phrase means nothing. We specify **exact guarantees**.
- A 2-of-3 threshold system (requires 3 ESP32s; we have 1)
- Zero-forensic-footprint (impossible on standard mobile OS)

### Honest MVP State (September 2025)
| Component | Status | Gap to Production |
|-----------|--------|-------------------|
| ESP32 firmware (Design B) | ✅ Working | No TLS, no secure element, no attestation |
| Smart contract (Base Sepolia) | ✅ Deployed | No policy engine, no revocation, no threshold |
| Host script (Python) | ✅ Working | No encryption, no signing, no key management |
| Frontend (browser) | ✅ Working | HTTP only, no integrity on HTTP, no CSP |
| IPFS retrieval | ✅ Working | Gateway fallback, no private retrieval |

**Bottom line:** MVP proves the *architecture*. Every cryptographic guarantee is **currently absent**. This document specifies how to add them.

---

## 2. THREAT MODEL (BRUTAL HONESTY)

### Adversary Capabilities We Assume
| Capability | Assumed? | Notes |
|------------|----------|-------|
| Passive network sniff (WiFi/cellular) | ✅ YES | Default |
| Active MITM on WiFi/cellular | ✅ YES | Default |
| Compromised phone OS (root/jailbreak) | ✅ YES | Default |
| Physical access to phone (forensics) | ✅ YES | Cellebrite, GrayKey |
| Physical access to ESP32 (clone/replace) | ✅ YES | **Critical gap in MVP** |
| Malicious IPFS gateway | ✅ YES | Pinata/Cloudflare could lie |
| Blockchain reorg (testnet) | ✅ YES | Base Sepolia not finality-guaranteed |
| Insider at Pinata/Alchemy | ✅ YES | Metadata leakage |
| Side-channel on ESP32 | ⚠️ PARTIAL | Power/EM analysis possible |

### Guarantees We **DO NOT** Claim
- ❌ "Untraceable" — carrier sees phone IP
- ❌ "Zero forensic footprint" — browser caches, swap, screenshots exist
- ❌ "Unbreakable" — 4-digit PIN = 10,000 guesses (public chain = offline brute)
- ❌ "Air-gapped" — ESP32 connects to internet via phone hotspot
- ❌ "2-of-3 threshold" — only 1 ESP32 available

### Guarantees We **DO** Claim (Post-Production)
| Guarantee | Mechanism |
|-----------|-----------|
| Retrieval requires physical proximity to authorized node | ESP32 session nonce + hardware button |
| File integrity verifiable end-to-end | AES-GCM tag + on-chain SHA-256 commitment |
| Authorization policy immutable once deployed | Base L2 smart contract |
| Compromised long-term key ≠ past sessions | Double Ratchet per session |
| Node compromise detected | Remote attestation via secure element |

---

## 3. SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE (SINGLE ESP32)

### 3.1 High-Level Data Flow

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                           PROJECT AETHER — SINGLE ESP32 OVERVIEW             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    HOST                          ESP32 (Single Node)                PHONE
    ────                          ─────────────────────             ─────
     │                                │                              │
     │  Encrypt + Sign + Upload       │                              │
     │  ──────────────────────────►   │                              │
     │           (Pinata IPFS)        │                              │
     │                                │                              │
     │  Register on-chain             │                              │
     │  ──────────────────────────►   │                              │
     │     (Base Sepolia)             │                              │
     │                                │                              │
     │                         ┌──────▼──────┐                       │
     │                         │  Aether-Setup│  (Phone connects)   │
     │                         │     AP       │                     │
     │                         └──────┬──────┘                       │
     │                                │                              │
     │                         Provision to                          │
     │                         Phone Hotspot                         │
     │                                │                              │
     │                         ┌──────▼──────┐                       │
     │                         │   STA Mode  │  (Joins phone net)    │
     │                         │  (Internet) │                       │
     │                         └──────┬──────┘                       │
     │                                │                              │
     │                         mDNS: aether-node.local               │

python --version                 # ≥ 3.11
node --version                   # ≥ 20

platformio --version             # ≥ 6.1
idf.py --version                 # ESP-IDF ≥ 5.0

# Python deps (host)
pip install -r host/requirements.txt

# Node deps (frontend)
cd frontend && pnpm install

# Foundry deps (contracts)
cd contracts && forge install
```

---

## 2. CONTRACT DEPLOYMENT

### 2.1 Networks

| Network | Chain ID | RPC URL | Explorer |
|---------|----------|---------|----------|
| Base Sepolia (Test) | 84532 | `https://base-sepolia.g.alchemy.com/v2/<key>` | `https://sepolia.basescan.org` |
| Base Mainnet (Prod) | 8453 | `https://base-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/<key>` | `https://basescan.org` |

### 2.2 Deployment Script (Foundry)

```bash
# contracts/Deploy.s.sol
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
pragma solidity ^0.8.20;

import "forge-std/Script.sol";
import "../src/AetherPolicy.sol";

contract DeployScript is Script {
    function run() external {
        vm.startBroadcast(vm.envOr("DEPLOYER_PK"));
        
        AetherPolicy policy = new AetherPolicy();
        
        // Register host as admin (deployer)
        // Authorize gates will be done separately via ProvisionGates.s.sol
        
        vm.stopBroadcast();
        
        console.log("AetherPolicy deployed at:", address(policy));
    }
}
```

```bash

forge script Deploy --rpc-url $BASE_SEPOLIA_RPC --broadcast --verify -vvvv

```

```bash
# 1. Verify contract on BaseScan
forge verify-contract <ADDRESS> AetherPolicy --chain-id 84532 --etherscan-api-key $BASESCAN_KEY

# 2. Set initial policy (if needed)
cast send <ADDRESS> "setPolicy(bytes32,Policy)" <file_id> <policy_json> --rpc-url $BASE_SEPOLIA_RPC --private-key $ADMIN_PK

# 3. Record deployment
echo "CONTRACT_ADDRESS=<ADDRESS>" >> .env.production
echo "DEPLOY_TX=<TX_HASH>" >> .env.production
echo "DEPLOY_BLOCK=<BLOCK_NUMBER>" >> .env.production

**The Brutal Answer (Memorize This):**

> **"A mobile app gives you *remote access* — anyone with the APK and PIN retrieves from anywhere. The ESP32 adds a *physical proximity requirement*: you must be at the device to authorize the session. That's a fundamentally different trust model."**

## The Three Technical Reasons (Ranked)

| Reason | Mobile App | ESP32 Hardware Gate |
|--------|------------|---------------------|
| **1. Proximity Enforcement** | GPS (spoofable), QR (clonable), Bluetooth (relayable) | **Physical button press + session nonce** — cannot be relayed |

| **3. Key Isolation (Future)** | Keys live in app process memory — dumpable via frida/root | **ATECC608B secure element — keys *never leave* the chip** |

> **"The phone is the *rendering endpoint* — it needs internet, screen, CPU. The ESP32 is the *authorization endpoint* — it decides *whether* the phone gets the session. An app cannot enforce physical presence. Hardware can."**

> **"Yes. The phone renders the file. The ESP32 *authorizes the decryption key release*. Same principle as an HSM — the HSM doesn't render the document, it authorizes the key. The ESP32 is a $12 HSM for file access."**
